newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Investors disenchanted with F J Benjamin.
newsitem.headline: Investors disenchanted with F J Benjamin.

text.p: F J Benjamin Holdings Ltd's shares fell on Thursday to below their initial public offer price of Singapore $0.80 for the first time since it was listed in November.
At 0745 GMT, the shares were trading around S$0.795, down S$0.045 on a turnover of 743,000 shares.

Luxury fashion retailer F J Benjamin left investors with a sour after taste after it reported a surprising 30 percent profit drop in net profit to Singapore $3.7 million for the half year ended December 31, 1996, analysts said.
Analysts said they called a sell on the stock after the results. The shares have since fallen over 30 percent.
The retailer, which has the agency for Guess, Gucci and other fashion brands, had registered over 90 percent earnings growth in 1995 before it went public.
F J Benjamin said its half-year results were affected by poor performance in its Australian operations.
The company told analysts earlier this week it did not mislead investors in the run-up to its listing.

"We had told analysts earlier we had forecast a loss for Australia but did not expect the severity of the loss," said general manager Wong Ai Fong. She added its Australian problems were well documented in the listing propsectus.
But analysts remained unconvinced and have downgraded the company's full year earnings to less than S$10 million compared to the previous consensus estimate of S$13.8 million.

"What was unexpected was the sharp losses. As a result, most investors have lost confidence in the company. There is no way they are going to meet the full year target," said one analyst with a local brokerage house.
